# Beamly

- Category: complement
- Checked: 2026-09-26
- Primary docs: https://beamly.com/

> **Verified 2026-09-26 (P0-03).** This file is the research-pass evidence for one vendor. Pricing, IAB certification and Apple HLS partner cells were rechecked against primary sources; corrections are marked inline. IAB status comes from the [IAB Tech Lab compliance registry](https://iabtechlab.com/compliance-programs/compliant-companies/). Apple's own partner search ([podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search](https://podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search)) redirects to an Apple ID sign-in, so partner status is attributed to the vendor or trade press, not an Apple list (checked 2026-09-26). The summary and comparison are in [`../vendors.md`](../vendors.md).

## Rebrand / identity check

Beamly is the rebranded successor to **Podcastpage.io** (not "Podpage," a separate, unrelated competitor). Beamly's own site states: "Podcastpage.io is now Beamly: a brighter home for podcasters to build, publish, and monetize the show and everything around it," and confirms continuity for existing users: "All existing users keep their current plan and pricing. Everything you use today works exactly as before." ([Podcastpage.io is now Beamly](https://beamly.com/podcastpage-is-now-beamly/), 2026-09-26). The rebrand was announced October 2025 and covers expansion beyond podcasting into video, courses, and digital products ([Beamly launch press release via Podnews](https://podnews.net/press-release/beamly-launch) (third-party), 2026-09-26).

Beamly explicitly distinguishes itself from **Podpage** (podpage.com) as a separate, competing product: "Podpage and Beamly (formerly Podcastpage.io) both help podcasters publish a website, but they are built very different." Per Beamly's comparison page, Podpage is template-based, episode-focused, has no native monetization or built-in analytics, and "builds a website from a podcast RSS feed" only (i.e., relies on an external host), whereas Beamly offers a drag-and-drop builder, native hosting, memberships, courses, and analytics ([Podpage vs Beamly](https://beamly.com/vs/podpage/), 2026-09-26). This is vendor-authored comparison copy, so treat the characterization of Podpage itself with caution, but the fact that they are distinct companies/products is clear.

## Does Beamly host media itself?

**Both.** Beamly offers native podcast/video hosting (upload episodes and media, and "Beamly generates and manages your RSS feed") and also supports "imported" podcasts connected via an external RSS feed from any other host, which stay in sync with the source feed: "Imported podcasts are connected via an external RSS feed that always stay in sync from the source feed, and you can use any podcast hosting provider as Beamly supports all of them." ([Podcast Website Builder](https://beamly.com/features/podcast-website-builder/), 2026-09-26; [Podcast Hosting Platforms](https://beamly.com/podcast-hosting-platforms/), 2026-09-26).

## Integration surface

- **API:** No public REST/GraphQL API found in Beamly's marketing site or Help Center category list. **Undocumented.** [Beamly Help Center](https://docs.beamly.com/) (2026-09-26)
- **Webhooks:** Not found in any page fetched. **Undocumented.**
- **Export formats:** RSS feed import/sync (both directions implied — connecting an existing RSS feed, or generating one from Beamly-hosted episodes) is the main documented interchange format. No CSV, bulk-media-download, or full-account-export documentation was found. **Undocumented** beyond RSS. [Podcast Hosting Platforms](https://beamly.com/podcast-hosting-platforms/) (2026-09-26)
- **SSO / auth:** No SSO/SAML mentioned anywhere reviewed. **Undocumented.**
- **Lock-in risks:** (1) No documented API/webhooks/bulk export beyond RSS sync — member/subscriber data portability is unaddressed in public docs. (2) Analytics are proprietary and not IAB-certified, so download/listener numbers may not be portable or directly comparable to a certified host's numbers if Relay ever needs certified reporting. (3) Redirect guidance is one-directional (into Beamly); no public documentation confirms Beamly will 301-redirect a feed on departure, which is the standard mechanism for retaining subscribers when leaving a host — this is a real risk for lock-in on the RSS feed URL if a podcast is _hosted_ (not just imported) on Beamly. [Podcast & Website Analytics](https://beamly.com/features/analytics/) (2026-09-26); [How to migrate your podcast RSS feed](https://beamly.com/how-to-migrate-your-podcast-rss-feed-or-change-podcast-hosts/) (2026-09-26)

## Narrative (≤150 words)

Beamly (formerly Podcastpage.io, distinct from the competitor Podpage) is a website-and-monetization layer that can optionally also host media — closer to Relay's "complement" category than a full hosting replacement, though its Business plan ($64/mo) does bundle native audio/video hosting, private RSS feeds, memberships with 0% platform fees, and drag-and-drop multi-show sites. It's weak on exactly what Relay needs most: no documented approval/review-before-publish workflow, no public API or webhooks (RSS sync is the only interchange point found), analytics that are IAB-compliant but explicitly not IAB-certified, and no confirmed Apple HLS video partner status. Comments/community features are absent from its own marketing. Redirect support appears to only be documented for migrating _in_, raising a lock-in concern for any feed hosted directly on Beamly rather than imported. It's a reasonable off-the-shelf front-end/monetization layer, not a governance or hosting backbone.

## Research notes

- `https://docs.beamly.com/category/integrations` returned HTTP 404; could not confirm exact Integrations article contents (Zapier/Stripe/YouTube integrations are referenced on the marketing homepage instead).
- No page found that explicitly lists Beamly among Apple's official HLS video hosting partners; Apple's own partner-directory tool content was not retrievable via fetch, so this is based on the visible text of Apple's overview page plus third-party (Sounds Profitable) coverage — flagged as **undocumented/unconfirmed** rather than "not supported."
- IAB Tech Lab's compliant-companies list page did not return a readable roster via fetch; relied on Beamly's own explicit statement ("IAB-compliant, but not certified") rather than cross-checking the IAB list directly.
- Pricing page fetch returned annual-billing figures ($18/$30/$64); did not independently confirm the monthly (non-annual) list price for each tier.
- No mention of "beta," "waitlist," or "US-only" restrictions found on any page reviewed.
